# Contributing

## Build

Java 17 or later and Maven 3.9 or later (the enforcer checks both). From the repository root:

```
mvn -q -B clean verify
```

This builds the six modules and runs every test, the JSR-385 TCK included. The modules are described in
[README.md](README.md); the design is in [docs/DESIGN.md](docs/DESIGN.md).

AI coding agents follow [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) (`CLAUDE.md` links to it).

## Generated files

The typed quantities in `uom-jsr/src/main/java/org/tinygears/uom/jsr/quantity`, the catalogs `SI`, `USCustomary`,
`Imperial`, `CGS`, `ESU`, `EMU`, `Gaussian` and `Information` in `uom-jsr/src/main/java/org/tinygears/uom/jsr/systems` and
[docs/UNITS.md](docs/UNITS.md) are generated by `uom-codegen` from `data/quantity-types.txt` and the `.units` files in
`data/`, and are committed; so are the native API's types and catalogs in
`uom/src/main/java/org/tinygears/uom/quantity` and `uom/src/main/java/org/tinygears/uom/systems`, generated from the
same files and `data/quantity-relations.txt`. Never edit them by hand. After changing `data/` or the generator,
regenerate:

```
mvn -q -B -Pgenerate -pl uom-codegen -am process-classes
```

`-am` builds `uom` and `uom-jsr` first, the generator's test dependencies; when their committed generated sources do
not compile (a generator change that renames what they use), install the engine and run the profile without `-am`:
`mvn -q -B install -DskipTests -pl uom-engine` and `mvn -q -B -Pgenerate -pl uom-codegen process-classes`.

The output is deterministic: running it on an unchanged tree changes nothing. `GeneratedSourcesUpToDateTest` fails
when `data/` and the committed files disagree, and the generator refuses to overwrite a file that does not carry its
header. Generated Java files start with the license header (see Formatting) followed by
`// Generated by uom-codegen from data/<files>; do not edit.`

## Formatting

The Java sources are formatted by the [Spotless](https://github.com/diffplug/spotless) Maven plugin with the Eclipse
formatter profile `config/eclipse-java-formatter.xml` (from the Open VSX project: 4 spaces, 120 columns, one argument
per line once a call wraps; unlike Open VSX it joins lines, so the formatter alone decides the line breaks, and it wraps
`extends` and `implements` onto one continuation line), the import order `config/import-order.importorder` (`java` and
`javax`, the others, `org.tinygears.uom`, then static imports) and the license header `config/license-header.txt`.
`mvn verify` runs `spotless:check` and fails on unformatted code; fix it with

```
mvn -q -B spotless:apply
```

The generator formats its output itself with the same profile, import order and header (`JavaFormatter`, through the
Eclipse JDT jars the Spotless step uses), so regenerated files are already formatted and `spotless:check` covers them
too; when you change the Eclipse version in the parent POM, change the JDT versions in `uom-codegen/pom.xml` with it.
Spotless leaves the header of `package-info.java` and `module-info.java` alone: write it there by hand.
`LicenseHeaderTest` checks every Java file. The `.mvn/` directory marks the repository root, so the configuration files
resolve from any module. Spotless skips files it has formatted before (`target/spotless-index`) and does not notice a
change of the files in `config/`: after changing them, run `mvn -q -B clean spotless:apply`. `.git-blame-ignore-revs`
lists the commits that only reformatted code; `git config blame.ignoreRevsFile .git-blame-ignore-revs` makes `git blame`
skip them.

## Tests

- Every change comes with tests; a bug fix with a test that fails without the fix.
- Tests assert exact values (exact strings, exact counts), not just "not null" or "contains".
- The build compiles with `-Xlint:all -Werror`: fix a warning, or suppress it on the smallest element (a field or a
  method) with a comment that says why.
- `ApiSurfaceTest` pins the public API to `docs/api/public-api.txt`. A deliberate API change rewrites the file with
  `mvn -B verify -Duom.writeApi`, and its diff is part of the change ([docs/DESIGN.md](docs/DESIGN.md), section 8).
- `mvn test -pl <module>` without `-am` takes the other modules from `~/.m2`, which may be stale: `ApiSurfaceTest`
  (in `uom-jsr`, for `uom-engine`, `uom` and `uom-jsr`) then compares an old `uom` or `uom-engine` jar. Add `-am`, or
  run `mvn -q -B install -DskipTests` first.
- `DocsSnippetsTest` runs the `units`, `units-error` and `java` blocks of `README.md`, `docs/NATIVE.md`,
  `docs/JSR.md`, `docs/CUSTOM-UNITS.md` and `SECURITY.md`: a `java` block compiles against
  `uom`, a `java jsr` block against `uom-jsr`, and a `units` block loads with both, which must agree. Keep them true
  when the behaviour changes.
- Release checks: `bash scripts/check-pom.sh` (POM metadata and release profile; `--self-test` proves its checks
  fail), `bash scripts/check-javadoc.sh` (no javadoc warnings in the published modules),
  `bash scripts/verify-release.sh` (release artifacts, reproducibility, jlink and a consumer project; uploads nothing;
  `--self-test` proves its checks fail) and `bash scripts/check-workflows.sh` (the CI workflow and dependabot
  configuration). [scripts/README.md](scripts/README.md) lists what each script checks.

Before a pull request, run what the CI runs (`mvn -B verify` on JDK 17, 21 and 25, the rest on JDK 21):

```
mvn -B verify
mvn -B -Pgenerate -pl uom-codegen -am process-classes
git diff --exit-code && test -z "$(git status --porcelain)"
bash scripts/check-pom.sh
bash scripts/check-javadoc.sh
bash scripts/check-workflows.sh
bash scripts/verify-release.sh --require-jlink
```

The workflow is `.github/workflows/ci.yml`; `bash scripts/check-workflows.sh` checks that it runs exactly these
commands, with a read-only token and no deploy step. `--require-jlink` needs a JDK that can link (Temurin can).

## Pre-commit hooks

`.pre-commit-config.yaml` runs cheap local checks, each only when the commit touches the files it reads:

- end of file, mixed line endings and trailing whitespace (fixed in place);
- `shellcheck` on the scripts and `zizmor` (from severity low) on the workflow and dependabot configuration;
- `spotless:apply` on the Java sources, and the regeneration of the generated sources from `data/` (both fix in
  place, so a hand edit of a generated file is reverted and the commit stops);
- `scripts/check-pom.sh` on a POM change and `scripts/check-workflows.sh` on a change under `.github/`;
- on the commit message, `scripts/check-commit-msg.sh`: the subject starts with a prefix of the conventions below.

It works with [prek](https://github.com/j178/prek) or [pre-commit](https://pre-commit.com/); each fetches the hook
versions pinned in the file and needs `mvn` and `python3` on the path:

```
prek install            # once: the pre-commit and commit-msg hooks
prek run --all-files    # check the whole tree
```

A run over the whole tree takes about 15 seconds. `check-javadoc.sh` (a clean release build) and the tests are not
hooks; `mvn -B verify` and CI stay the gate.

## Conventions

- Every `.java` file starts with the license header of `config/license-header.txt` (`LicenseHeaderTest` checks it;
  `spotless:apply` writes it); scripts carry `# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0` after the shebang. Contributions are licensed under the
  [Apache License 2.0](LICENSE).
- Code comments are short (one to three lines) and state what the code cannot: a constraint or a reason.
- Commit subjects use a conventional prefix: `feat:`, `fix:`, `perf:`, `refactor:`, `chore:`, `docs:`, `test:`,
  `style:`, `build:`, `ci:`, optionally with a scope (`fix(engine):`) or `!`. The body says what changed and why. No
  emojis.
- Documentation is concise and technical; every statement must match the code and the commands.
- Releases are made by the maintainer only, following [docs/RELEASING.md](docs/RELEASING.md).
